clue.text: Pinto pony's head that's smooth

indicators.note: the head of the pony is its opening letter, picked out here

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is
bald means smooth, without hair or tread

explanation.surface: A horse lover remarks that a patchy pony has a sleek, smooth head.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a horse with patches of two colours, the same as a piebald.

clue.text: In waters off Japan, island Marines attacked initially

definitions.text: In waters off Japan, island Marines attacked initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the seven words before it

explanation.surface: A war report of US Marines storming a Pacific island near Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of the first seven words spell the island, and the whole clue describes the 1945 battle there, so it is an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Iwo Jima is a Japanese island where US Marines landed in a famous 1945 assault.

clue.text: Stand in western cemetery, badly neglected

indicators.note: neglected tells us that part of the cemetery's name is left out

parts.note: Boot Hill is the name for a graveyard in Wild West towns
ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A stall stands in a rundown cemetery out in the Wild West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western' here means a cowboy film or story, giving BOOT HILL; 'neglected' drops ILL, leaving the stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A booth is a small stall or stand at a fair or market.

clue.text: Huge lad cracked up? Yes

indicators.note: cracked suggests the letters of the phrase are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a big boy burst out laughing, and is told he did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' rearranges HUGE LAD, and the whole clue, a lad who cracked up, describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up is to burst into laughter, so one who cracked up chortled.

clue.text: Top singer strangles Mozart's first quaver

indicators.note: strangles means grips round the neck, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a treble sings the highest part in a choir

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A soprano chokes on the opening note of a Mozart piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quaver' looks like a musical note in this musical surface, but here it is the verb meaning shake.
explanation.definitionFit: To quaver is to shake or quiver, especially of a voice.

clue.text: Is fascinating teacher coming up to collect doctor?

indicators.note: to collect means to take in, so one piece holds the other
coming up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: pupils call a male teacher sir
a vet is an animal doctor

explanation.surface: A question about whether a charismatic teacher arriving to pick up a doctor holds attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that grips attention is said to hold one spellbound, which this verb expresses.

clue.text: Writer's trade, lacking energy, is on the wane, say

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: lacking tells us a letter is removed

parts.note: market can mean trade, as in a market for goods
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: say indicates a word that sounds like the one before it

parts.note: a wane is a decline

explanation.surface: An author laments that his line of work is in decline without any energy.
explanation.walkthrough: WAIN, an old word for a cart, sounds like 'wane'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of the American novelist Samuel Clemens.

clue.text: Limo left officer in pub

indicators.note: in signals the officer is placed inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
Col is short for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: A chauffeur leaves the limousine to drop a colonel at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln is an American make of luxury car often used as a stretch limousine.

clue.text: A quarter past eight, time to recall some lights here

definitions.text: A quarter past eight, time to recall some lights here

parts.words: A quarter past eight, time to recall some lights here
parts.note: in the 24-hour clock a quarter past eight in the evening is written with two numbers, and those two numbers are also entries in this grid; the year also marks a battle anniversary

explanation.surface: An evening hour when someone remembers lamps being switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: The year the puzzle appeared was 600 years after Agincourt (1415); the two numbers also point to 20 and 15 in this grid, the tax and the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-fifteen is how 20:15, a quarter past eight in the evening, is read aloud on the 24-hour clock.

clue.text: Did it originally die out twice?

definitions.text: Did it originally die out twice?

indicators.note: twice means the pair of letters is repeated
originally means taking the opening letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a creature became extinct on two occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'die out' give two letters, doubled by 'twice'; the whole clue suggests the famously extinct bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless bird of Mauritius is the classic example of an extinct species.

clue.text: Resolute peacekeepers fly across state

parts.note: UN peacekeepers belong to the United Nations

indicators.note: across means one word stretches over and around the other

parts.note: to wing is to fly
to aver is to state or assert

explanation.surface: Determined UN troops fly over a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resolute is steady and firm, never faltering.

clue.text: Thigh ordered by the quarter? Half that

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A diner orders thigh meat sold by the quarter, then wants only half of that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the compass point beside the rearranged letters. 'Half that' refers back to 'the quarter': half a quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Half of one quarter is one part in eight.

clue.text: Jacques cut midday music in bars

indicators.note: cut means splits, so the surname goes into the middle of the time

parts.note: noon is midday
Jacques Tati was a French film comedian and director

explanation.surface: A Frenchman interrupts lunchtime music in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs but means the measures of written music.
explanation.definitionFit: Written music is set out on staves divided into measures, the system of written symbols.

clue.text: Carefree youth, once a pint-sized star in States

indicators.note: in places the star inside the verb

parts.note: says means states
Alan Ladd was a Hollywood film star noted for being short

explanation.surface: A tiny celebrity spent his carefree youth in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like the USA but is the verb; Alan Ladd was a 1950s Hollywood star of famously short stature.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Shakespeare means one's inexperienced early years, now gone.

clue.text: King competed thus in battle

parts.note: a tennis King playing an opponent is, in dialect, against someone on a tennis court; it also describes Henry V fighting at a famous battle

explanation.surface: A monarch took part in combat in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: AGIN is dialect for against; Billie Jean King played against rivals on court, while Henry V fought this 1415 battle in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt is the 1415 battle in northern France won by Henry V of England.

clue.text: Charter catamaran to be deployed around Gulf

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround another
to be deployed means the letters are arranged in a new formation

parts.note: G is the radio code letter for golf, spelt here as gulf

explanation.surface: Hire a catamaran to sail around the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charter' looks like a verb meaning hire, but it defines the great 1215 charter of English liberties.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1215 document King John sealed is England's most famous charter of rights.

clue.text: Move on board, heading off to find compass

indicators.note: heading off means the front letter is removed

parts.note: a gambit is an opening move in chess

explanation.surface: Someone makes a move on a chessboard, setting off to find a compass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compass' looks like a navigation tool but means scope or range.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit and compass both mean the extent or scope of something.

clue.text: Best timekeepers in West Street, Rhode Island

parts.note: Mae West was a Hollywood actress
RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: Top watchmakers are found on West Street in Rhode Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timekeepers' suggests clocks but means conductors, who keep the beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Great conductors beat time for an orchestra, and the Italian plural honours the masters.

clue.text: After short period Monk, say, ignores one drummer

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: time means a period

indicators.note: ignores means one letter is left out

parts.note: Thelonious Monk was a jazz pianist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: After a brief spell, a monk ignores a percussionist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monk' looks like a religious figure but is the jazz pianist Thelonious Monk.
explanation.definitionFit: A timpanist plays the kettledrums in an orchestra.

clue.text: Toll devised during peace as source of revenue

indicators.note: during means inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: pax is Latin for peace

indicators.note: devised means the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A toll was introduced in peacetime to bring in money.
explanation.walkthrough: The poll tax was a hugely unpopular UK local tax of 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: A head tax charged on each person raises money for a government.

clue.text: Boss lives over old workshops

parts.note: a stud is a raised knob, also called a boss

indicators.note: over means one piece goes around another

parts.note: is means lives, exists

explanation.surface: A manager lives above some old workplaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager but means a stud, a knob on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Studios are workrooms for artists or broadcasters.

clue.text: US writer's wife ousted by college poet

indicators.note: ousted by means one letter is replaced by another

parts.note: Saul Bellow was an American novelist

explanation.surface: An American author's spouse is pushed aside by a college poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilaire Belloc was an Anglo-French writer known for comic verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilaire Belloc wrote Cautionary Tales and other verse.

clue.text: Leaves box and coaches close to street

parts.note: to coach is to teach

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a box behind and trains people near the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, but it is tea leaves, and the definition is a box for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a wooden crate for shipping tea.

clue.text: Where Lucy danced with me in 70s?

definitions.text: Where Lucy danced with me in 70s?

indicators.note: danced means the letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recalls where Lucy and they danced in the 1970s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'danced' rearranges LUCY and ME; the Lyceum in London was a famous ballroom and music venue in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lyceum in London's Strand was a ballroom and concert venue.

clue.text: See 16 Across
How tanners work to maximise profit, i.e. hell for leather?

definitions.text: How tanners work to maximise profit
definitions.meaning: tanners process hides, so working on a whole skin is the way to get most from it
hell for leather means as fast as possible

explanation.definitionFit: A pelt is an animal skin, and the idiom means at top speed, flat out.

clue.text: Check rule head of government scrapped

indicators.note: scrapped means removed from the word

parts.note: to reign is to rule

indicators.note: head of takes the opening letter

explanation.surface: Curbing the rule of a government leader by scrapping him.
explanation.definitionFit: To check is to restrain, as a rider does with a horse's strap.

clue.text: It quelled unrest in port, thanks to court

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: Disorder in a port was ended by a court ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act of 1714 was read aloud to disperse crowds in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1714 law was read out to order rioters to disperse.

clue.text: Picked up tyre as well as another car part

definitions.meaning: tyre sounds like tire, which means to wear out
the pipe carrying fumes from the engine

explanation.definitionFit: To wear someone out is to drain them, and the car's fume pipe is also called that.
